Schema v2 maps only a local blood-pressure observation to FHIR R4 Observation under the official BP profile and emits the LOINC code-system version (2.83) on panel/component Coding entries. The implementation pins UCUM specification 2.2 locally, but FHIR R4 Quantity has no version element, so the UCUM release is not carried on the wire and no UCUM terminology validation is claimed. The Patient reference must be supplied explicitly and is not resolved or created. UCUM mm[Hg], effective/issued instants and unknown/not-measured reasons are preserved. Non-blood-pressure inputs and unsupported references/units fail closed. The mapper omits free-text notes and recorder identity, marks the result preliminary, and does not establish FHIR server interoperability, clinical validation or patient identity.

Schema v1 previews only an exact FHIR R4 blood-pressure Observation subset in memory, binding caller-declared source base, FHIR release, jurisdiction and expected Patient reference while retaining resource metadata, terminology versions, displays, timestamps and distinct component absent reasons. Unsupported fields, unsupported statuses, mismatched identities, invalid timestamps, unknown absent reasons, comparators or unsupported units are held. The decoded numeric preview is not a lossless archive of the original JSON decimal spelling; no data is persisted, no CDSS algorithm consumes the preview, and no network SMART exchange, server conformance or clinical validity is established.

Schema v3 packages one to twelve chronological blood-pressure Observation resources as an immutable FHIR R4 collection Bundle using the versioned local BP mapper and an explicitly supplied Patient reference. The Bundle is a local preview artifact, not a transaction, server exchange, patient-identity resolution or full clinical-record export.

Schema v5 binds ordered caller or built-in P0 inputs, projected local records, merged FoodItem content, merge collisions, jurisdiction context, merge policy and tie-break into an in-memory result snapshot with a canonical SHA-256. It adds a local projection query audit for the six queryTable reads, including table names, no-WHERE/no-ORDER-BY query shape, adapter-returned record IDs and order, row counts, canonical row-set digests, and implemented selection and last-wins rules; only the volatile _synced_at field is excluded from row hashes. The reads remain sequential and are not transaction-scoped, and caller query and filters are not captured. Projected foods retain available per-nutrient observation IDs and evidence plus linked source-document ownership, license notes, source metadata and payload-text SHA-256, linked preparation/sampling scope, and recorded concept/variant crosswalk evidence. FDC source-reported foodPortions fields are projected as separate FoodPortionEvidence with source document and food identifiers; the original complete raw payload text is not copied into candidate records. The existing registry checksum is retained as supplied and the payload digest identifies only persisted raw-payload UTF-8 text after ingestion, not a complete catalog release. Non-exact nutrient rows and portion records are evidence only and do not alter legacy ranking. Crosswalk confidence is recorded metadata, not validated match accuracy. The snapshot reports unavailable upstream catalog release, caller-side query/filters, selected serving, validated food matching and nutrient conversion, sample counts and quantitative measurement uncertainty. It is not a catalog freeze, does not establish rank stability and is not a persisted record.

Schema v1 is a non-persisted preview bound to a captured candidate snapshot, an explicitly named FoodData Central Foundation portion record, and a selected exact nutrient observation from the same source food and document. It applies the per-100-g edible-portion formula only when source type, identifiers, basis, unit, scope, and any paired source extrema agree. Other data types and incomplete or conflicting evidence are held. The preview has no ranking effect, does not select a user serving, and treats source sample extrema as extrema rather than confidence or probability limits; portion-weight uncertainty is not quantified. Each serialized report carries a canonical SHA-256 over the result fields using lexically sorted object keys and an explicit IEEE-754 binary64 hexadecimal tag for every JSON numeric value, so Dart and JavaScript reproduce the same digest independently. The digest binds the explicit portion locator and candidate-snapshot digest.

Schema v1 records the six sequential CdssDatabase.queryTable operations used by food projection, their no-WHERE/no-ORDER-BY shape, returned primary-key IDs and order, row counts, content hashes and exact implemented food selection and last-wins filters. Table hashes exclude only volatile _synced_at fields. Reads are not transaction-scoped and do not establish an atomic database snapshot; caller-side query/filters and upstream catalog release identity remain unavailable. Raw row payloads are hashed but are not copied into the audit.

Schema v1 is a bounded synthetic-only fixture with exact context keys, explicit nullable inputs and offset-bearing timestamps, a fixed synthetic subject, authored expected target decisions/winners/missing fields, and exact rule-pack source/version/content binding. Unknown schemas, unsupported fields or units and malformed values are rejected. Absent expectations are not verification; changing the case invalidates prior run evidence.

Schema v1 freezes complete declarative rule JSON and binds its source, bundle version, canonical content digest and unique per-rule versions. Imported bindings must match the content. This is an isolated current-engine replay pack, not an installed knowledge database, authenticated review, source-document archive or clinical activation approval. The synthetic-json-binary64-v1 profile type-tags every node, sorts object keys and represents finite safe-range numeric values as binary64 bytes; integral doubles and signed zero are normalized for desktop/web identity. Malformed Unicode and out-of-range numbers reject.

Schema v1 reports exact case/input/rule content identities, current engine identity, explicit execution status selection and expected/actual assertion results. A binding mismatch or missing/excluded trace cannot verify an assertion. No expectations means notVerified. It does not restore historical executables or source-document bodies and does not establish clinical correctness or independent review.

Schema v1 is a strict synthetic-only suite of one to sixteen independently bound rule cases with unique IDs and a bounded encoded size. Unknown or missing fields, duplicate IDs, empty or oversized suites and unsupported versions fail closed. The suite is a test input and carries no persistence or activation authority.

Schema v1 records sequential per-case current-engine results, independent case status counts, selected binding and explicit no-persistence/no-activation boundaries. Missing assertions and binding mismatches do not count as passes. The report is synthetic engineering evidence, not clinical validation or independent review.

Schema v1 reports added/removed/changed IDs, exact JSON Pointer field changes with presence flags, complete array order and same-version content-drift warnings. Null is distinct from absence; limit violations reject the comparison without truncation. This report establishes structural differences only, not semantic equivalence, clinical impact or source authenticity.

Schema v1 content-addresses NLM RxNorm Current Prescribable Content release metadata, official filename, publisher checksum, release notes, enumerated scope and terms. The archive was not downloaded or locally verified, no terminology rows or product mappings are included, and absence from the active subset remains unresolved, not retired. Release drift holds for review. This metadata pin is not bound into algorithm identity and does not establish RxNorm/FHIR conformance, dose appropriateness, prescription validity, administration, adherence or clinical correctness.

Schema v1 content-addresses a source-currency observation for the official FAO/INFOODS tagnames page. The page reports a 2022-10-20 update, records additions through 2010, and still marks proposed tags and a consolidated Excel list as coming soon; this does not establish a complete current vocabulary or released tagname package. The remote page was not archived or hashed, no tagname rows or mappings are downloaded or bundled, and mapping remains on hold until a versioned complete source is reviewed. This metadata artifact does not establish INFOODS conformance or clinical correctness.

Schema v1 compares caller-supplied old/current catalog record-set captures using exact codes and explicit, snapshot-bound transition evidence. Record-set and diff SHA-256 values are deterministic content identities only: they are not signatures, publisher archive verification, or proof of source completeness. Changed-code classification trusts caller-declared review and license states plus a well-formed evidence digest and matching capture bindings; those declarations and references are not independently authenticated. Retirement is explicit, absent codes stay unresolved, and name similarity never creates a mapping. Split, merge, ambiguous, stale, unreviewed, unlicensed and missing evidence remain held for an owner decision. The Data Integrity page accepts this schema as an ephemeral local preview: it recomputes capture digests, rejects unknown fields, and does not mutate saved medication records. A separate explicit local action scans active medication identities and intake identity fields and emits aggregate exact-source-code reference counts only. These rows do not bind the source catalog release, so matches are potential references rather than confirmed affected records; multiple changed-code matches remain unattributed. The result exposes no record identifiers, names, or dose details, and the scan is not persisted, sent, or applied. The UI lists at most 20 changed codes and clears on input or relevant owner-state edits. No mapping is applied, persisted, or verified as a publisher release; unresolved updates are not wired to runtime algorithm abstention. Catalog completeness, terminology conformance and clinical correctness are not established.

Schema v1 is an ephemeral challenge preview for exactly one fixed synthetic information card. It binds the input digest and canonical card SHA-256, requires one bounded reason code and rationale, exists only in the current diagnostics page memory, is not saved or transmitted, and does not change the response or rule outcome. Real health or personal data must not be entered. This contract provides no human-factors, clinical-validation, or CDS Hooks conformance evidence.

Schema v2 accepts one typed FHIR R4 Patient-scoped Observation template with an explicit, versioned ValueSet and integer count comparator. It generates CQL and a draft Library with Patient and code-filtered Observation data requirements, translates to ELM with pinned CQF CQL, and evaluates fixed in-memory synthetic cases through pinned cql-execution and cql-exec-fhir. Unsupported fields, modifiers and mismatched synthetic outcomes fail closed. The translation terminology warning remains explicit; the fixed synthetic ValueSet is not an external terminology resolution. No network, real patient data, persistence, FHIR validation or runtime activation occurs, and the artifact makes no clinical validity claim.

Schema v1 binds a mechanistic result to the exact offline evidence-currency registry version and digests, UTC as-of time, sorted provider and claim identities, disposition, explicit boundary, and binding digest. Unknown or missing fields, unsupported schema, malformed values, unsorted identities or digest mismatch fail closed. The digest is tamper-evident content identity, not a signature, source-validity claim, durable history, clinical validation or treatment recommendation.

Grammar v4 binds the exact local unit mapping and rejects unsupported, ambiguous or adjacent Unicode unit text. It preserves the original note and holds nonconforming expressions from result-affecting algorithms; parsing is not a dose recommendation.

Version 1 records ascending Meal.effectiveOccurredAt ordering, grams per meal from computeTotals, and arithmetic mean with zero for an empty list. It is a local descriptive aggregation, not a clinical adequacy or outcome claim.

Version 1 is an in-memory bounded source-range stress-test report bound to the exact candidate snapshot digest. Missing, stale or observed order-change evidence withholds ranked presentation; a no-change report does not establish full rank stability, confidence, probability or clinical benefit.

Version 1 projects an owner-entered intake as a FHIR R4 MedicationStatement with unknown status, display-text medication identity and an explicit Patient reference. Local timestamps without a retained offset become date-only. Record identifiers, dose receipts, terminology codes and product details are excluded; the output does not verify administration or clinical correctness.

Version 1 binds a bounded synthetic-only suite checkpoint to suite identity and SHA-256 digest, selected rule binding, execution mode and unique completed cases. Unknown fields, versions, oversized inputs and malformed identities fail closed. Checkpoints grant no persistence or runtime activation authority and are not clinical validation.
